data.title: Lint
data.tagline: Lint is static checking that uses source rules to find suspicious patterns and consistency problems without running the full program.
data.learningOutcome: You can use lint as source-rule checking and know it cannot replace runtime and user-journey verification.
data.description: Lint can locate unused variables, clear mistakes, or unhandled promises and make the warning disappear after a correction. It finds source-level risks early. Clicking a button and confirming save results or API responses still need build, tests, or manual verification.

learning.assumes: You have seen an editor show a warning or error beside a code line.
learning.outcome: You can use lint as source-rule checking and know it cannot replace runtime and user-journey verification.

distinctions.label: Unit test
distinctions.explanation: Lint finds suspicious source patterns without running the complete program. A Unit Test executes one code unit and checks its actual result.

explanation.title: It checks source shapes and conventions
explanation.text: Rules find unused variables, risky patterns, or team-inconsistent code without starting the full application. Results point to a file and line for quick pre-commit correction.

explanation.title: Static passing is not correct running
explanation.text: Lint does not click buttons, wait for networks, or confirm database writes. Put it in CI as an early check, then use tests and acceptance for actual behavior.

data.boundary: Lint is not a unit test, build, or user acceptance. It analyzes source rules without executing the full program; passing only says current rules did not trigger, not that behavior, performance, or real configuration is correct.

lessonPractice.title: A PR’s lint passes, but clicking save shows no feedback. What is the most accurate judgment?

options.label: Source rules found no issue; operate or test the save flow and feedback next
options.feedback: Correct. Passing lint does not prove button events, network requests, or page state are right.

options.label: Passing lint means saving is fully accepted
options.feedback: Static checking did not execute a user action, so it cannot supply that evidence.

options.label: Since errors can still happen, do not run lint
options.feedback: Lint still catches another class of issues early; it simply should not be mistaken for all verification.

data.agentPrompt: Enable and fix lint reports for unused variables and unhandled promises. Put lint in PR checks, but still test the save button afterward: click, wait, success feedback, and failure feedback all need confirmation.
